subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should `disableBoundaryAwareCache` become a public model compat contract that defaults on for DeepSeek, or should the same behavior remain an internal DeepSeek transport policy without a user-facing key?
rationale: Both directions can fix the measured regression, but they create different long-term configuration, naming, upgrade, and provider-extension contracts that repository policy reserves for maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve scoped compat contract
options.body: Default the behavior only for DeepSeek, preserve explicit `false`, and allow other proven prefix-cache providers to opt in through model compat metadata.

options.title: Internalize DeepSeek policy
options.body: Remove the public key and apply the transformation solely through internal DeepSeek capability detection, accepting less operator control.

options.title: Select config-free sibling
options.body: Use the broader sibling approach only after it covers the production agent transport and supplies comparable live provider proof.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped compat contract
recommendation.body: Default the behavior only for DeepSeek, preserve explicit `false`, and allow other proven prefix-cache providers to opt in through model compat metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to both the cache-boundary design and the affected OpenAI-compatible transport seam.
